interim_publication_reason: Fitch assessment reported by Reuters on the financing and investment implications of new U.S. advanced-chip controls in Asia-Pacific data centres.
Reuters reporting, based on people familiar with the companies, of potential Z.AI and Moonshot AI model-development delays.
Reuters investigation identifying MiniMax in an AI inference data-handling and URL-access investigation, with MiniMax and Atlas Cloud statements reviewed.
Reuters poll forecast of South Korean November export growth, supported by Korea Customs Service preliminary first-20-day trade data.

source_audit.verification_note: Four current-window Reuters reports were opened and checked against publication timestamps and material claims. Six earlier government, company or technical-research documents were opened as supporting evidence. Anonymous-source claims, company statements and research-firm findings are separately attributed. No 100% verification claim is made.

research_findings.topic: Asia-Pacific advanced-chip controls and data-centre financing
research_findings.caveat: The BIS rule is primary regulatory text. Fitch's view is reported by Reuters; no direct Fitch publication was retrieved.
Z.AI and Moonshot release timing was not company-confirmed. The BIS rule does not independently verify internal model schedules.

MiniMax says full conversations were not retained and no broader prompt/response disclosure was found in examined requests. Feishu activity and code-download attempts remain unresolved; Dragos's original report did not name MiniMax.
The 96.8% figure is a Reuters poll forecast, not an official November result. The customs figures cover 1-20 November and are preliminary.
